title: Set the Music app's own volume to a given level

source.licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0; ported by reference (our own instruction, setup and checks; no source text copied)
source.changes: Instruction written in our own words. The target level is a param; the source's 50 is one pick, and each pick keeps the source's tolerance (more than 4 below or above fails, as in 45 < v < 55). The source activated Music on an AMI snapshot with whatever volume it held; here setup keeps Music's own volume, sets it to 100 so the agent must change it, and teardown puts it back and quits Music.

setup.why: Keep Music's own volume for teardown, set it to 100 so the agent has to lower it, and bring Music to the front.

instruction: In the Music app, find where Music's own volume is set, and set it to {{vol.want}}%.

checks.why: Music's sound volume (its own slider, not the Mac's output volume) is within 4 of {{vol.want}}, the source's tolerance. Setup left it at 100, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: tell application "Music" to get sound volume

teardown.why: Put Music's own volume back and quit Music.

oracle.why: Set Music's volume, as its slider does.

argv: tell application "Music" to set sound volume to {{vol.want}}
